questions.q: Tomas Arguelles is famously known for designing the 'Heacock Building' in pre-war Manila. What was the primary function of this landmark structure?
o: The premier department store of its time
questions.n: Located on the Escolta, the Heacock Building was a symbol of Manila's thriving pre-war retail and commercial scene.

questions.q: Which sporting and social venue in Manila, known for horse racing, featured a grandstand and clubhouse designed by Tomas Arguelles?
o: The Wack Wack Golf and Country Club
The Manila Jockey Club (San Lazaro Hippodrome)
questions.n: Arguelles designed the iconic pre-war facilities for the San Lazaro race track, a hub of Manila social life.

questions.q: Tomas Arguelles worked as an assistant to which famous American architect during the early years of the Bureau of Public Works?
questions.n: Arguelles was part of the early wave of Filipino talent working alongside the American architects who laid Manila's urban foundation.

questions.q: The 'Reliance Building' in Manila is another of Arguelles' notable works. What architectural style did he often employ for these early 20th-century commercial structures?
o: A transition between Neoclassicism and early Art Deco
questions.n: His commercial works often featured the clean lines and restrained ornamentation that bridged the gap between these two eras.

questions.q: True or False: Tomas Arguelles was a pioneer in the 'Maestro de Obra' (Master Builder) tradition before the formal professionalization of architecture in the Philippines.
questions.n: Like many of his generation, he bridged the gap between the Spanish-era builders and the modern licensed architects.

questions.q: Tomas Arguelles was a key figure in the development of which famous Manila street, often referred to as the 'Wall Street of the Philippines' before World War II?
questions.n: Arguelles designed several major commercial landmarks along this street, which was the country's primary business and luxury retail hub.

questions.q: Arguelles is credited with being one of the first to form a professional architectural partnership. What was the name of his influential firm?
questions.n: Arguelles established a professional firm that paved the way for modern corporate architectural practices in the Philippines.

questions.q: Before the formal Architect's Law was passed in 1921, what was the Spanish title for builders like Arguelles who performed architectural duties?
questions.n: This title, meaning 'Master of Works,' was given to individuals trained in construction and design before the professional title of 'Architect' was regulated.

questions.q: True or False: Tomas Arguelles primarily focused on designing religious cathedrals and large-scale parish churches during his career.
questions.n: Arguelles was distinct from Spanish-era architects because he focused on the needs of the rising business class and urban commerce.

questions.q: Which material became more prevalent in the commercial buildings designed by Arguelles as Manila transitioned into the modern era?
questions.n: Reinforced concrete allowed for the multi-story commercial designs and the stylized Art Deco elements Arguelles implemented.

questions.q: The San Lazaro Hippodrome grandstand was an important project for Arguelles. What was a primary design requirement for such a structure?
o: Creating a small, intimate residential feel
Ensuring clear sightlines for large crowds
questions.n: A grandstand's primary function is to provide a tiered view of the racing track for thousands of spectators.

questions.q: How did Arguelles' work as a 'consultant' differ from his colleagues like Juan Arellano who worked in the Bureau of Public Works?
o: He refused to use any modern American techniques
He only worked on projects outside of Manila
He often worked with private developers and business owners
He worked only as a carpenter without any design input
questions.n: While many architects focused on government buildings, Arguelles was a pioneer in the private sector and commercial real estate.

questions.q: The 'Reliance Building' is often cited as a transition piece in Arguelles' career. This transition refers to the move from:
o: Classic Roman styles to the 'Steel and Glass' high-rise
Heavy Spanish ornamentation to cleaner, more geometric Modernism
questions.n: His work bridged the gap between the decorative past and the functional, geometric Art Deco style.

questions.q: What role did Tomas Arguelles play in the professionalization of Filipino architects?
o: He led a movement to ban all American architects
He was the first Filipino to graduate from a European school
He wrote the first textbook on Philippine architecture
He was among the first group of professionals to be officially recognized under the 1921 Architect's Law
questions.n: Arguelles represents the generation that transformed from skilled craftsmen into legally recognized professionals.

questions.q: True or False: The Heacock Building was considered one of the most modern and fire-resistant buildings of its time in Manila.
questions.n: The use of concrete and modern fire-proofing standards was a major selling point for high-end commercial properties on the Escolta.
